KP 1. Calculating the Velocity of a Particle
1.?

The position x of a particle at time t is given by x(t)=tet. Calculate the velocity at time t.

E
Fri, Aug 7th @ 9:06 PM|Elapsed: 1:12Correct

The velocity is the derivative of the position function x(t) with respect to time: v(t)=dxdt=ddt(tet)=et+tet=(t+1)et

2.?

The position x of a particle at time t is given by x(t)=4t3+3t2+2. Calculate the velocity at time t.

E
Fri, Aug 7th @ 9:06 PM|Elapsed: 0:26Correct

The velocity is the derivative of the position function x(t) with respect to time:

v(t)=dxdt=ddt(4t3+3t2+2)=12t2+6t

KP 2. Calculating the Velocity of a Particle at a Particular Moment
3.?
The position s(t) of a particle at time t is given by s(t)=−2csc⁡t,0<t<π. Calculate the velocity at time t=π4.
v(π4)=
2
E
Fri, Aug 7th @ 9:09 PM|Elapsed: 2:13Correct

First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

v(t)=dsdt=ddt(−2csc⁡t)=2csc⁡tcot⁡t

To calculate the velocity at t=π4, we substitute t=π4 into the velocity function above: v(π4)=2csc⁡(π4)cot⁡(π4)=2⋅2⋅1=2

4.?

The displacement s (in meters) relative to a fixed origin O of a particle moving in a straight line along the x-axis is given by the equation s(t)=e3t−2, where t is the time, measured in seconds. Find the position and velocity of the particle at the initial moment of time t=0s.

M
Fri, Aug 7th @ 9:13 PM|Elapsed: 4:03Correct

To calculate the initial position, we substitute t=0 it into the equation s(t)=e3t−2: s0=s(0)=e3(0)−2=e−2=1e2m

Now, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function: v(t)=dsdt=ddt(e3t−2)=3e3t−2

To calculate the velocity at t=0s, we substitute t=0 into the velocity function above: v0=v(0)=3e3(0)−2=3e2m/s

KP 3. Calculating the Speed of a Particle at a Particular Moment
5.?

The position s(t) of a particle (in millimeters) at time t seconds is given by s(t)=9t−t3,t≥0. Calculate the speed of the particle when t=2s.

E
Fri, Aug 7th @ 9:16 PM|Elapsed: 0:24Correct

First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function: v(t)=dsdt=ddt(9t−t3)=9−3t2

When t=2, the velocity is v(2)=9−3(2)2=9−12=−3.

Therefore, the speed is |−3|=3mm/s.

6.?
The position s(t) of a particle (in meters) at time t seconds is given by s(t)=6sin⁡t−8cos⁡t,t>0. Calculate the speed of the particle when t=3π2s.
The speed of the particle is
8
m/s.
M
Fri, Aug 7th @ 9:18 PM|Elapsed: 2:19Correct

First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function: v(t)=dsdt=ddt(6sin⁡t−8cos⁡t)=6cos⁡t+8sin⁡t

When t=3π2, the velocity is v(3π2)=6cos⁡(3π2)+8sin⁡(3π2)=6(0)+8(−1)=−8.

Therefore, the speed is |−8|=8m/s.
